statement.p: Evaluate \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}}\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\,dA, where \mathcal{D} is the domain in Figure 4

static.solution:
{\mathcal{D}}_1 and {\mathcal{D}}_2 the regions enclosed by the circles x^2+y^2=36 and (x-3)^2+y^2=9.
Therefore, \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} \sqrt{x^2+y^2} \,dx \,dy = \int\!\!\int _{{\mathcal{D}}_1} \sqrt{x^2+y^2} \,dx \,dy - \int\!\!\int _{{\mathcal{D}}_2} \sqrt{x^2+y^2} \,dx \,dy \quad (\mathbf{1}) We compute the integrals on the right hand-side.
{\mathcal{D}}_1:
\begin{array}{ll} F: x^2+y^2=36\quad \\R_f=6 \end{array}
The circle x^2+y^2=36 has polar equation r=6, therefore {\mathcal{D}}_1 is determined by the following inequalities: {\mathcal{D}}_1: \,0\le \theta \le 2\pi,\ 0\le r\le 6 The function in polar coordinates is f( x,y )=\sqrt{{x}^2+{y}^2}=r. Using change of variables in the integral gives \int\!\!\int _{{\mathcal{D}}_1} \sqrt{{x}^2+{y}^2} \,dx \,dy= \int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{6} r\cdot r \,dr \,d\theta = \int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{6} {r}^2 \,dr \,d\theta=\int_0^{2\pi } \frac{{r}^3}{3}\bigg|_{r=0}^{6}\,d\theta = \int_0^{2\pi } \frac{216}{3} \,d\theta = \frac{432\pi }{3} \quad (\mathbf{2}) {\mathcal{D}}_2 :
\begin{array}{lll} G: (x-3)^2+y^2=9\\R_f=6 \quad R_g=3 \\ 0 \le r \le 6\cos\theta\end{array}
{\mathcal{D}}_2 lies in the angular sector -\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}.
We find the polar equation of the circle (x-3)^2+y^2=9: {(x-3)}^2+{y}^2= {x}^2-6x+9+{y}^2= {x}^2+{y}^2-6x+9=9\begin{array}{lll} {x}^2+{y}^2=6x\\ {r}^2=6r \cos \theta\\ r=6 \cos \theta \end{array} Thus, the domain {\mathcal{D}}_2 is defined by the following inequalities: {\mathcal{D}}_2:\,-\frac{\pi}{2}\le\theta\le\frac{\pi}{2},\ 0\le r\le 6 \cos \theta We use the change of variables in the integral and integration table to obtain \int\!\!\int _{{\mathcal{D}}_2\,} \sqrt{{x}^2+{y}^2} \,dx \,dy= \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \int_0^{6 \cos \theta } r\cdot r \,dr \,d\theta= \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \int_0^{6 \cos \theta } {r}^2 \,dr \,d\theta=\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \frac{{r}^3}{3}\bigg|_{r=0}^{6\cos \theta}d\theta= \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \frac{216\, \cos^3\theta }{3} \,d\theta= 2 \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{216\, \cos^3\theta }{3} \,d\theta=\frac{432}{3}\left(\frac{\cos^2\theta \sin \theta }{3}+\frac{2}{3} \sin \theta \right)\bigg|_{\theta =0}^{\pi/2}= \frac{432}{3}\cdot \frac{2}{3} \sin \frac{\pi }{2}= \frac{864}{9}\quad (\mathbf{3}) Substituting (\mathbf{2}) and (\mathbf{3}) in (\mathbf{1}), we obtain the following solution: \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} \sqrt{{x}^2+{y}^2} \,dx \,dy= \frac{432\pi }{3}-\frac{864}{9} \approx 356.389
